Question 1

(a) Plot Pr(Y=k|X=2) for k=0 ,1,...,15.
```{r}
lambda = exp(1 + 0.5*2)
plot(dpois(0:15, lambda = lambda), ylab = "Pr(Y=k|X=2)", xlab = "k")
```

(b) What is the most plausible value for Ywhen X=2 ?
```{r}
which.max(dpois(0:15, lambda = lambda))
```

(c) Construct a 95% prediction interval for Y.
```{r}
qpois(c(0.025, 0.975), lambda = lambda)
```

Question 2: ISL Chapter 4: Exercise (applied) 13(e)-(i).
```{r}
# Import the data
library(ISLR2)

# Split the Dataset
train = (Weekly$Year < 2009)
Weekly_09_to_10 = Weekly[!train, ]

# The Logistic Regression Model
mod_log = glm(Direction ~ Lag2, data = Weekly, family = binomial, subset = train)

# Confusion Matrix and Overall Error Rate
predicted_prob_log = predict(mod_log, Weekly_09_to_10, type = "response")
predicted_direction_log = rep("Down", length(predicted_prob_log))
predicted_direction_log[predicted_prob_log > 0.5] = "Up"
Direction_09_to_10 = Weekly$Direction[!train]

table(predicted_direction_log, Direction_09_to_10)

mean(predicted_direction_log==Direction_09_to_10)
```

(e) Repeat (d) using LDA.
```{r}
library(MASS)
mod_lda = lda(Direction ~ Lag2, data = Weekly, subset = train)

# Confusion Matrix and Overall Correct Prediction Rate
lda.pred = predict(mod_lda, Weekly_09_to_10)
lda.class = lda.pred$class
table(lda.class, Direction_09_to_10)
mean(lda.class==Direction_09_to_10)
```

(f) Repeat (d) using QDA.
```{r}
mod_qda = qda(Direction ~ Lag2, data = Weekly, subset = train)

# Confusion Matrix and Overall Correct Prediction Rate
qda.class = predict(mod_qda, Weekly_09_to_10)$class
table(qda.class, Direction_09_to_10)
mean(qda.class==Direction_09_to_10)
```

(g) Repeat (d) using KNN with K = 1.
```{r}
library(class)
set.seed(1)
train.X = Weekly[train, ]$Lag2
test.X = Weekly[!train, ]$Lag2
train.Direction = Weekly[train, ]$Direction

# make sure train.X and test.X has the same dimension
dim(train.X) = c(length(train.X), 1)
dim(test.X) = c(length(test.X), 1)

knn.pred = knn(train.X, test.X, train.Direction, k=1)

# Confusion Matrix and Overall Correct Prediction Rate
table(knn.pred, Direction_09_to_10)
mean(knn.pred==Direction_09_to_10)
```

(h) Repeat (d) using naive Bayes.
```{r}
library(e1071)
mod_nb = naiveBayes(Direction ~ Lag2, data = Weekly, subset = train)

# Confusion Matrix and Overall Correct Prediction Rate
nb.class = predict(mod_nb, Weekly_09_to_10)
table(nb.class, Direction_09_to_10)
mean(nb.class==Direction_09_to_10)
```

(i) Which of these methods appears to provide the best results on this data?
The logistic regression model and LDA provide the best results since they have the highest correct prediction rate of 0.625.
